identity.title: Emergence of high-mass stars in complex fiber networks (EMERGE): III. Fiber networks in Orion

paper_type_evidence.quote: We surveyed seven prototypical star-forming regions in Orion as part of the EMERGE Early ALMA Survey.

targets.name: OMC-1, OMC-2, OMC-3, OMC-4 South, LDN 1641N (Orion A)

question.value: How is the dense gas in seven low- to high-mass Orion star-forming regions organised into velocity-coherent fibers, and what are the fibers' masses, lengths, kinematics, virial state and link to star formation?

evidence.quote: We aim to investigate the dense gas organisation prior to the formation of stars in a selected sample of regions within Orion.

analysis_steps.goal: Fiber masses, line masses, kinematics, virial ratio

method.value: Sum N(H2) over pixels for M; sigma_nt from linewidth minus thermal; m_vir=2 sigma_tot^2/G

evidence.quote: $$m_{\rm{vir}} = \frac{2(c_{\rm{s}}(T_{\rm{K}})^2 + \sigma_{\rm{nt}}^2)}{G}=\frac{2\sigma_{\rm{tot}}^2}{G}.$$

assumptions.value: Factor of 3 omitted in m_vir (1D dispersion); mu_N2H+=29; inclination 45 deg for gradient estimates

evidence.quote: We instead kept the estimate given by Eq. ([\[mvirial\]](#mvirial))

analysis_steps.goal: Associate protostars and correlate fiber density with dense gas mass

method.value: Star-forming fibers have protostars within one beam; linear fit of Sigma(fibers) vs M_tot

evidence.quote: We identified the star-forming fibers in our sample as those structures with protostars enclosed within less than one $\theta_\mathrm{beam}$

evidence.loc: 5.4 Fibers as the preferred organisation of the dense gas in clouds
evidence.quote: This correlation reads as $\Sigma (fibers) \sim 0.26~M_\mathrm{tot}$ according to a linear fit to the data.
supervised fitting of the spectra through customised GILDAS/CLASS routines
applying the Hierarchical Friends-In-Velocity (HiFIVe) algorithm
with the publicly available routine FilChap
we identified and characterised a total of 152 velocity-coherent fibers in our survey
with a corresponding median value for the whole sample of 0.09 pc
$\langle m/m_{\rm{vir}}\rangle\sim1.1$ (dotted line) for the star-forming fibers and $\langle m/m_{\rm{vir}}\rangle\sim0.55$
one third of the fibers in the survey (50) is star forming with two thirds of the protostars in our fields (82) associated to them

findings_qualitative.value: Fibers have similar mass and length distributions and (trans-)sonic motions in all regions

evidence.quote: the masses and lengths of these objects show similar distributions and consistent median values, as well as (trans-)sonic motions, in all of our targets

claims.hypothesis: Fibers are the preferred organisation of dense gas across low- to high-mass regions
claims.experiment: HiFIVe on ~170,000 N2H+ spectra in seven Orion regions
claims.result: 152 fibers, >95% of components in structures, similar M, L, sonic motions
claims.finding: Fibers are the common organisational unit

evidence.quote: highlights these small-scale filamentary sub-structures as the preferred organisational unit for the dense gas

claims.hypothesis: Star-forming fibers are closer to virial
claims.experiment: Compared m/m_vir of fibers with and without protostars
claims.finding: Massive near-virial fibers host most protostars

evidence.quote: The virial ratios for the star-forming fibers are consistently shifted towards higher values compared to those of non-star-forming fibers.

claims.hypothesis: Fiber surface density scales with dense gas mass
claims.experiment: Linear fit of Sigma(fibers) to M_tot
claims.result: Sigma ~0.26 M_tot within a factor of 2
claims.finding: Fibers generated in constant proportion per unit dense gas

evidence.quote: All regions in our survey reproduce this tight correlation within less than a factor of 2 difference

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Original Hacar+2018 column density thresholds [26,44,66] Av judged insufficient for the wider dynamic range

evidence.quote: these thresholds cannot efficiently sample the whole column density range

evidence.quote: acknowledging that the 3D velocity dispersion is likely higher than the one presented
